text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated streaming tail latency observed on /v1/stream endpoints. p95 ~ 1.2s (ok), p99 ~ 6.8s (breach). Affected region: us-west-2. Bot has paged the on-call rota.

sam (oncall): acked. I'm looking. paging now to eng-runtime + eng-sre.

alex (eng-runtime): on it. any customer reports?

irene (support): got 3 tickets saying 'stream freezes for ~6s then resumes' across different customers, no errors in client logs, mostly SSE clients.

maria (eng-sre): I'm seeing a clear spike in tail latency around 12:05 UTC, coincides with a surge of concurrent streaming sessions (~1.6x normal). p50/p95/p99 from prometheus: p50=120ms, p95=1.2s, p99=6.8s.

sam (oncall): initial hypothesis: proxy (edge) timeouts/backpressure causing buffering + slow consumers. Can someone grab proxy/nginx logs and runtime metrics?

alex (eng-runtime): pulling logs from runtime nodes. quick grep shows retransmit/backpressure entries:

```
2026-03-12T12:05:14Z runtime-node-12 stream: client=cid-9ab upstream_write_blocked=true kv_cache_size=24 pending_bytes=65536
2026-03-12T12:05:18Z runtime-node-7 stream: backend_send_latency=12ms proxy_write_err=EPIPE downstream_buffered=47872
2026-03-12T12:05:22Z runtime-node-7 stream: stall_detected duration=6250ms reason=slow-consumer
```

alex (eng-runtime): looks like the runtime is marking stalls due to downstream blocking. Not an application compute issue.

lee (eng-platform): nginx edge metrics show increasing proxy_queue_depth and some 504 upstream timeout spikes at the same window. config currently: proxy_read_timeout=60s, proxy_send_timeout=60s, proxy_buffer_size=8k.

maria (eng-sre): Prom query I ran: `sum(rate(streaming_response_latency_seconds_bucket{le="1",job="runtime"}[5m]))` etc. but here's a clearer one: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_response_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` -> 6.8.

sam (oncall): mitigation suggestions? quick toggles we can do without deploys: increase proxy buffers/timeouts, reduce per-connection batching, route some traffic to dedicated pool, enable non-stream fallback for affected customers.

alex (eng-runtime): We can reduce the runtime's max response chunk size to 16KB from 64KB on the fly (hot-config) which reduces head-of-line blocking when downstream is slow. I can apply to a subset.

lee (eng-platform): I can increase nginx proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size and bump proxy_read_timeout to 90s in the edge ASGs; will push a config change to the control plane (no code deploy) -> ian. Doing canary to 2 edge nodes now.

maria (eng-sre): Also recommending to enable prefix caching for the top 10% of repeated prompts to reduce on-demand tokens. That can take load off runtime temporarily.

sam (oncall): action list (short):
- alex: hot-change runtime chunk_size to 16KB for 25% nodes (in progress)
- lee: edge config canary bump (proxy buffers, read timeout) (in progress)
- maria: roll up a temporary alert to mute noisy p95 alerts but keep p99 pagers (so we don't flood)
- irene: add support-facing status note that we're investigating streaming stalls (do not call customers yet)

alex (eng-runtime): applied chunk_size hot-config to 25% of runtime nodes at 12:14 UTC. Metrics will take ~30s to reflect.

lee (eng-platform): canary edge config pushed to 2 nodes at 12:15 UTC, no immediate errors. Rolling to 20% now.

maria (eng-sre): I muted the p95 pager at 12:16 UTC, leaving p99 and error rate.

sam (oncall): any immediate change in p99?

maria (eng-sre): early signal: p99 dropped from 6.8s -> 4.1s after chunk_size change on canary subset, then -> 3.2s as canary expanded and proxy buffers increased. still above SLO (2s p99).

irene (support): customers are reporting fewer freezes now, two said "much better".

alex (eng-runtime): follow-up finding: heavy clients with very small read windows (mobile clients) create significant backpressure — we should prioritize a change to allow smaller write chunks per connection. Also seeing some slow-client TCP hysteresis where kernel buffer sizes on proxies hit highwater.

lee (eng-platform): I'm going to temporarily route a small % of traffic from hosted API to dedicated-capacity pool (cold) for the largest customers to take pressure off the shared edge path. Doing a 5% route at 12:23 UTC.

maria (eng-sre): after routing and canary rollout complete, p99 now at ~1.9s at 12:30 UTC — below the SLO. We'll keep monitoring for 30m.

sam (oncall): great. start of handoff in 30m to next oncall. Please summarize actions and candidate postmortem bullets.

alex (eng-runtime): summary actions we've done:
- Hot-config: reduced runtime chunk_size from 64KB -> 16KB (rolled to 100% over 8m)
- Edge config: increased proxy_buffer_size, proxy_busy_buffers_size, proxy_read_timeout -> rolled to 100%
- Traffic routing: temporarily shifted 5% of traffic for large tenants to dedicated pool
- Alerts adjusted to focus on p99

maria (eng-sre): postmortem bullets:
- Root cause hypothesis: burst of concurrent streaming sessions combined with high-share small-read clients caused proxy buffer exhaustion and downstream backpressure leading to long tail stalls.
- Contributing factors: default chunk size too large for conditions; edge buffers/timeouts conservatively tuned; no per-client backpressure shedding.
- Action items: adjust default chunk_size and make adaptive chunking; add per-client sliding window detection to drop/slow low-priority streams; improve edge autoscaling thresholds for queue depth; add unit test to simulate small-read clients.

irene (support): I'll send a status update to affected customers summarizing mitigation and next steps.

sam (oncall): handoff notes posted to pager duty and I'll escalate if p99 climbs > 2.5s again. Next oncall @maria at 12:58 UTC will take over.

alex (eng-runtime): leaving a note: runtime logs show no memory/CPU issues, purely backpressure. We'll prioritize adaptive chunking.

lee (eng-platform): follow-up: temporary rollback knobs are in the control plane: route-ratio and edge-buffer toggles. Documented in runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-backpressure (adding a short note).

maria (eng-sre): closing the pager at 12:40 UTC since p99 < SLO and trends stable. Will open an incident ticket with severity LOW and follow-up action items.

sam (oncall): thanks everyone. if anyone sees p99 climb again ping here and escalate. Good mitigation teamwork. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident resolved (auto) - duration 00:35:23, severity: LOW, postmortem: assigned to eng-runtime + eng-platform.
